fields.name: elev
fields.meaning: Surface (bed) elevation at the output time, relative to the model datum (sea level 0 unless the sea-level curve moves). float64. Shown as Z in the XDMF/ParaView file.
fields.range: Set by the input topography: about -11000 to +9000 m on Earth global meshes (examples: -6500 to +7300 m); a few hundred m to a few km on regional meshes.
fields.resolution: Point value; finer meshes resolve narrower valleys and higher peaks. Independent of dt except through the processes.

fields.name: erodep
fields.meaning: Cumulative erosion (negative) and deposition (positive) thickness since the start of the run, all processes included (rivers, hillslopes, marine, gravity currents, carbonate framework, coastal erosion, karst, ice). Not changed by uplift or flexure. float64, restart field. Shown as ED in ParaView.
fields.range: Grows with run time: tens to a few hundred m over 1 Myr regional runs (examples -220 to +300 m); -8000 to +17000 m extremes on global 10-100 Myr runs, with the median near 0.
fields.resolution: Cumulative thickness, so nearly independent of dt; extremes are sharper and larger on finer meshes (one-cell channels and depocentres).

fields.name: EDrate
fields.meaning: Net erosion/deposition thickness rate of the LAST time step before the output (river step plus the marine, hillslope, carbonate framework, coastal erosion and karst contributions). Not averaged over the output interval. float64, restart field.
fields.range: Typically 1e-6 to 1e-3 m/yr; incision up to ~1e-2 m/yr and marine/fan deposition up to a few 1e-2 m/yr at single cells (examples -0.025 to +0.059 m/yr).
fields.resolution: Rate over one dt (dt-averaged): a longer dt smooths short pulses and an implicit large-dt deposit spreads its rate over the step; peaks grow on finer meshes.

fields.name: FA
fields.meaning: Water discharge (flow accumulation of the net runoff, rain minus evaporation plus meltwater/baseflow) on the actual surface, routed with the multiple-flow-direction scheme. Floored at DISCHARGE_FLOOR (1e-8); marine nodes are set to 1.0 unless domain fast is on. float64, restart field.
fields.range: From rain x cell area at divides (1e3 to 1e7 m3/yr depending on cell size and rain) to 1e9-1e10 m3/yr for regional trunks and ~1e12-1e13 m3/yr for continental rivers on global meshes; 1 everywhere in the sea.
fields.resolution: The value at a given point of a channel is resolution independent (it is an area x rain), but the minimum (one cell) scales with dx^2 and hillslope cells carry less on finer meshes (flow spread by MFD). Rate: no dt dependence beyond the forcing.

fields.name: fillFA
fields.meaning: Flow accumulation through the lakes: FA on rivers, and on lake cells the water flowing into the lake (through-flow for a lake that spills, evaporated for a closed one). Not used by the erosion (FA is zero on lakes). float64, restart field.
fields.range: As FA on rivers; on lakes, their inflow (up to the discharge of the largest rivers for lakes on them). Before Nov 2026 lake cells held 10 % of the maximum discharge.
fields.resolution: Same as FA.

fields.name: sedLoad
fields.meaning: River sediment load (total, coarse plus fine) carried downstream through each node, from the sediment routing of the last step. Floored at DISCHARGE_FLOOR (1e-8). float64, restart field. Shown as SL in ParaView.
fields.range: 1e-8 (floor) on hillslopes without transport and in the sea; tens to 1e5 m3/yr in regional rivers (examples up to 8e5 m3/yr); 1e8 to a few 1e9 m3/yr for continental rivers on global meshes.
fields.resolution: Volumetric flux, so resolution independent along a channel in principle, but the eroded volume (hence the load) depends on resolution through the SPL drainage area on hillslopes and the resolved slopes; it reflects the last dt only.

fields.name: sea
fields.meaning: XDMF-only attribute (no HDF5 dataset): the sea level of the output time repeated on every node, for thresholding the ocean in ParaView.
fields.range: The sea-level curve value (0 m by default).
fields.resolution: Uniform; independent of mesh and dt.

fields.name: coords
fields.meaning: Node coordinates (x, y, z) of each partition, written once in h5/topology.p<rank>.h5 (float32). Flat meshes: planar x, y with z = 0; global meshes: Cartesian x, y, z on the sphere of radius domain:radius.
fields.range: Domain size; about +-6.378e6 m on an Earth sphere.
fields.resolution: Mesh geometry only.

fields.name: cells
fields.meaning: Triangle connectivity (three node indices, 1-based, int32) of each partition, in h5/topology.p<rank>.h5, written once.
fields.range: Integer indices from 1 to the number of local nodes.
fields.resolution: Mesh geometry only.

condition: unless domain: fast: True (written whenever depressions are filled)

fields.name: waterFill
fields.meaning: Water depth of lakes in closed depressions: the filled water level minus the bed elevation (0 outside lakes and in the sea). The code subtracts the bed (waterFilled -= hl), so it is a depth, not a water-surface elevation as the outputs page says. float32, not used on restart. With evaporation, a closed lake stands at the level where its evaporation balances its inflow.
fields.range: 0 almost everywhere; centimetres to tens of metres in lakes, up to 1e3-4e3 m in deep closed basins of global runs (examples: median 5-20 m among lake cells, maximum 3900 m).
fields.resolution: Depends on the depression volumes and the inflow of the last step; a larger dt fills pits faster. Finer meshes resolve more small pits.

condition: with the climate block (rain, evap) or a tectonics map with vertical displacement (uplift)

fields.name: rain
fields.meaning: Precipitation rate applied at the output time (the climate map or uniform value, or the orographic rain when the orography block is on). float32. Shown as Rain.
fields.range: Input forcing: 0 to a few m/yr (examples 0.0007 to 5.8 m/yr).
fields.resolution: Forcing, interpolated to the mesh; independent of dt. The orographic rain is solved on the mesh, so its smoothing scales with the mesh spacing.

fields.name: evap
fields.meaning: Evaporation rate of the current climate event (written only when an event defines evap_uniform or evap_map). float32. Shown as Evap.
fields.range: Input forcing: 0 to a few m/yr; calibration dependent.
fields.resolution: Forcing; independent of mesh and dt.

fields.name: uplift
fields.meaning: Vertical tectonic displacement rate in force (the tectonics event map, applied at the start of each step). float32. Shown as vTec.
fields.range: Input forcing: typically -1e-2 to +1e-2 m/yr (examples -0.01 to +0.0076 m/yr, uniform -0.0005 m/yr subsidence in the atoll example).
fields.resolution: Forcing; independent of dt (applied as uplift x dt each step).

fields.name: sedLoadF
fields.meaning: Fine (mud) part of the river sediment load; the coarse load is sedLoad - sedLoadF. Floored at 1e-8. float64, restart field. Shown as SLf.
fields.range: Between 1e-8 and sedLoad; examples up to 6.5e8 m3/yr on global meshes, about half the total load where the bedrock fine fraction is 0.5.
fields.resolution: As sedLoad.

fields.name: surfFineFrac
fields.meaning: Fine fraction (by bulk thickness) of the topmost non-empty stratigraphic layer: the composition exposed at the surface. float32.
fields.range: 0 (all coarse) to 1 (all mud); the bedrock value (1 - bedrock_coarse_frac) where no sediment covers it (examples median 0.4-0.7).
fields.resolution: Depends on the layer interval (strat) and dt: thin top layers make it vary faster; little mesh dependence.

fields.name: flexIso
fields.meaning: Cumulative flexural isostatic deflection since the start of the run (sum of each flexure solve's increment). float64, restart field.
fields.range: Tens of m on regional runs (examples -53 to +900 m: escarpment rebound reaches several hundred m), up to +-several km at extreme global load changes (examples -8900 to +3700 m).
fields.resolution: Cumulative, set by the load history; with flex_interval > 1 it is updated only every N steps. The flexural wavelength is resolved only when the mesh spacing is well below it.

fields.name: soilH
fields.meaning: Soil/regolith thickness (mobile layer above bedrock). float64, restart field.
fields.range: 0 on bare bedrock to a few m; examples median 0.2-0.9 m among soil cells, maximum about 18 m in hollows/deposits.
fields.resolution: State variable; production and creep depend on slopes, so steeper resolved slopes on fine meshes give thinner soils. Little dt dependence once at equilibrium.

fields.name: iceH
fields.meaning: Ice thickness from the Bahr scaling H = eheight x fwidth x Q^0.3 of the routed ice discharge. Floored at 1e-8 and set to 1.0 on marine nodes unless domain fast is on (a quirk of the writer). float64, restart field.
fields.range: 0 (1e-8) outside glaciers; tens to a few hundred m in valley glaciers (example max 114 m, median 29 m among ice cells).
fields.resolution: Diagnostic of the last step's ice discharge, not time integrated; follows FA-like resolution behaviour through Q^0.3 (weak).

fields.name: iceFA
fields.meaning: Ice discharge: the ELA accumulation routed downhill (glacial analogue of FA). float32.
fields.range: 0 outside glaciers; 1e4 to 1e7 m3/yr in valley glaciers (example max 1.9e7).
fields.resolution: As FA (area x accumulation rate).

fields.name: iceUb
fields.meaning: Basal sliding speed from the Glen sliding law on the ice thickness and surface slope; drives abrasion. float32.
fields.range: 0 off the ice; ~1 to tens of m/yr (example median 1.7, max 61 m/yr); calibration dependent (slide).
fields.resolution: Depends on the resolved slope, so faster on finer meshes over steep beds.

fields.name: iceAbr
fields.meaning: Vertical glacial abrasion rate E_g = Kg |u_b|^l (lateral wall erosion Kl not included). Zero when Kg = 0. float32.
fields.range: 0 to ~1e-3 m/yr (example median 5e-5, max 1.8e-3 m/yr); calibration dependent.
fields.resolution: Rate of the last step; inherits the slope dependence of iceUb.

fields.name: iceMelt
fields.meaning: Glacial meltwater delivered to the rivers where the ice melts out (ablation zone, terminus). float32.
fields.range: 0 except at the ablation zone; up to ~1e7 m3/yr per cell in the example.
fields.resolution: Volumetric flux; concentrated on few cells, so peak values per cell grow on coarser meshes.

fields.name: recharge
fields.meaning: Net groundwater recharge f_infil x max(0, rain - evap) (optionally reduced on slopes and fine sediment), zero under the sea, lakes and ice. float32.
fields.range: 0 to a fraction of the runoff: examples 0.003 to 0.3 m/yr.
fields.resolution: Forcing-like; independent of dt. Slope reduction (infil_slope_ref) makes it mesh dependent.

fields.name: wtable
fields.meaning: Water-table head (elevation of the saturated surface); pinned to the surface under the sea. float64, restart field.
fields.range: Follows the topography (examples 20 to 2200 m on land); equals elev in the sea. A few outliers far below the seafloor were seen on a global example (-21800 m), calibration dependent.
fields.resolution: Steady Dupuit solve each step, so independent of dt; finer meshes resolve valley-scale head gradients.

fields.name: wtdepth
fields.meaning: Depth of the water table below the surface z - h, clipped to [0, aquifer thickness]. 0 in the sea and at seepage faces. float32.
fields.range: 0 at seepage/valleys to the aquifer thickness (examples cap at 30, 50 or 100 m).
fields.resolution: As wtable.

fields.name: baseflow
fields.meaning: Seepage-return discharge re-injected into the rivers (land only, zero on marine nodes). Written with conserve_baseflow (default True). float32.
fields.range: 0 away from seepage nodes; 1e5 to 6e6 m3/yr per seepage cell in the examples.
fields.resolution: Volumetric flux concentrated on seepage cells; per-cell values scale with the upslope area draining to them.

condition: with the groundwater block and its nested duricrust block (duriOn)

fields.name: duricrust
fields.meaning: Duricrust thickness duriH, capped at max_thickness. float64, restart field.
fields.range: 0 to max_thickness (examples 5 and 20 m).
fields.resolution: Grows with time at the capillary fringe; with geochemistry the precipitation rate k_p is per year, so a large dt saturates it in fewer steps.

fields.name: induration
fields.meaning: Induration degree duriF = duriH / max_thickness, or the archived induration of an exhumed crust layer where larger. float32.
fields.range: 0 to 1.
fields.resolution: As duricrust.

fields.name: Karmor
fields.meaning: Erodibility armoring multiplier 1 - armor_max x duriF applied to K.
fields.range: 1 - armor_max (e.g. 0.1 or 0.02) to 1.
fields.resolution: As duricrust.

condition: with the groundwater geochem block (gwGeochemOn); riverSolute with river_load; marineSoluteInput with marine_coupling; crust_type and per-species fields with more than one species; crust_source with the provenance block

fields.name: solute
fields.unit: solute units per m3 of water
fields.meaning: Groundwater dissolved concentration summed over the species (steady transport solve of the step). float32.
fields.range: Calibration dependent (weatherability, source pool): examples 1e-7 to 1e-2, one ferricrete example up to 10.
fields.resolution: Steady per step, so independent of dt; depends on the resolved head gradients.

fields.name: soluteflux
fields.meaning: Dissolved export leaving the aquifer at seepage nodes (baseflow-carried), summed over species. The outputs page labels it m3/yr, which holds only when the solute is counted as a volume (for example solute_per_m3 = 1). float32.
fields.range: 0 away from seepage nodes; 10 to 1e7 per seepage cell in the examples; calibration dependent.
fields.resolution: Per-cell flux concentrated on seepage cells.

fields.name: crust_type
fields.meaning: Dominant crust-forming species per node (index in the species list, -1 = no crust). Integer stored as float32. Only with more than one species.
fields.range: -1 to number of species - 1.
fields.resolution: Categorical.

fields.name: crust_source
fields.meaning: Dominant source-rock (provenance) class of the solute that formed the crust (-1 = no crust). Integer stored as float32. With provenance.
fields.range: -1 to number of provenance classes - 1.
fields.resolution: Categorical.

fields.name: riverSolute
fields.meaning: River dissolved load: the seepage export (and karst dissolution of its species) routed down the drainage network per species and summed; accumulates downstream to the coast. With river_load. float32.
fields.range: 0 on dry hillslopes; up to 1e7-1e8 at river mouths in the examples; calibration dependent.
fields.resolution: Accumulated like FA, so resolution independent along trunks.

fields.name: marineSoluteInput
fields.meaning: River dissolved load entering the ocean at coastal and outlet exit nodes in the step (0 elsewhere). With river_load and marine_coupling. float32.
fields.range: 0 except at river mouths; up to 1e7-6e7 in global examples.
fields.resolution: Concentrated on mouth cells.

fields.name: solute_<name>
fields.unit: solute units per m3 of water
fields.meaning: Groundwater concentration of one species (one dataset per species, name from the species list). Only with more than one species. float32.
fields.range: Calibration dependent; examples 1e-7 to 1e-2.
fields.resolution: As solute.

fields.name: crust_<name>
fields.meaning: Cumulative crust thickness contributed by one species (precipitated mass x solid_volume per unit area), summed over the run; never reduced by erosion. Only with more than one species. float32.
fields.range: 0 to tens of m, up to ~240 m at single nodes in global examples; calibration dependent.
fields.resolution: Cumulative; the precipitation rate is per year so it grows with dt x steps.

fields.name: soluteflux_<name>
fields.meaning: Seepage export of one species. Only with more than one species. float32.
fields.range: Calibration dependent; examples up to 5e5.
fields.resolution: As soluteflux.

fields.name: riverSolute_<name>
fields.meaning: River dissolved load of one species. Only with more than one species and river_load. float32.
fields.range: Calibration dependent; examples up to 1e8.
fields.resolution: As riverSolute.

fields.name: gravDep
fields.meaning: Cumulative net thickness change from the marine gravity currents since the start of the run: deposit (positive) minus slope erosion and failure (negative). The code accumulates it every step (gravDep += deposit - erosion) and never resets it, so it is not the deposit of the step as outputs.rst says. float64, restart field.
fields.range: 0 on land and the shelf; metres to tens of m on slope aprons and basin floors (regional examples median 13-14 m, max 70-100 m; global examples up to a few hundred m to 5 km at single sink cells); negative to -10 to -400 m with erosion_length or failure_slope.
fields.resolution: Cumulative; the run-out solve uses exp(-dx/L), so deposits are mesh consistent when the run-out is several cells; spreading (deposit_spread, default two cell sizes) smooths peaks more on coarse meshes. Slope erosion is not meaningful on cells coarser than ~200 m.

condition: with the carbonate block (carbOn; needs dual lithology and marine deposition)

fields.name: carbProd
fields.meaning: Benthic carbonate production rate of the last step, all factories (framework plus the loose sand and mud handed to the marine routing), integrated over the step with the sea-level cap. float32.
fields.range: 0 outside the factories; up to the largest factory growth (default factories 800 m/Myr = 8e-4 m/yr; examples median 2e-5 to 6e-4, max 1.5e-3 m/yr).
fields.resolution: Rate averaged over dt: the accommodation cap reduces it when the step fills the water column (more at large dt). Depth-dependent factories make it sensitive to the resolved shelf width.

condition: with the pelagic block (pelOn; needs dual lithology)

fields.name: pelDep
fields.meaning: Settled (or, with resuspend, resuspended) pelagic thickness rate of the step: carbonate preserved above the CCD plus hemipelagic clay. Deposits thinner than DEPOSIT_FLOOR are carried over and appear in a later step. float32.
fields.range: 0 on land and below the CCD for carbonate; of the order of the input rain, a few m/Myr (examples up to 1.4e-5 m/yr, median 1-2e-6 m/yr).
fields.resolution: Rate of the last step; uniform input so little mesh dependence except the clay_decay length relative to the cells.

fields.name: sst
fields.meaning: Sea-surface temperature at the output time (event map or uniform value plus the curve anomaly). float32.
fields.range: Input forcing: about 0 to 30 degC (examples 0 to 29 degC).
fields.resolution: Forcing; independent of mesh and dt.

fields.name: waveE
fields.meaning: Relative wave energy weighted over the wave climate, from the upwind energy transport with fetch growth and shoaling dissipation; 0 on land and in wave shadows, 1 at full open-ocean energy. Recomputed when a factory or the coastal erosion needs it (otherwise the last computed field, zeros if never computed). float32.
fields.range: 0 to 1; open water 0.9-1 on flat meshes, lower in shadows and lagoons (examples 1e-4 to 1).
fields.resolution: Upwind first-order transport, so shadows and gradients are smeared over a few cells and sharper on finer meshes; independent of dt.

condition: with the coastal_erosion block (coastOn; needs waves and marine deposition)

fields.name: coastEro
fields.meaning: Cumulative wave erosion of cliffs and shallow seafloor since the start of the run (positive thickness removed). float64, restart field.
fields.range: 0 away from the coast; metres to tens of m on eroding coasts (examples median 1-15 m among eroded cells, max 6-270 m), capped by max_erosion per step.
fields.resolution: Cumulative; cliff retreat proceeds one cell at a time, so the eroded thickness depends on cell size: in the carbonate_terraces example the maximum was 6.6, 8.9 and 14.7 m at 50, 100 and 200 m spacing (coarser cells erode thicker).

condition: with the karst block (karstOn; needs lithologies)

fields.name: karstDiss
fields.meaning: Cumulative karst dissolution of the exposed carbonate lithologies since the start of the run (bulk thickness removed). float64, restart field.
fields.range: 0 outside exposed carbonates; rate x runoff x time, e.g. 50 m/Myr with rate 5e-5 and 1 m/yr runoff (example median 8 m, max 30 m).
fields.resolution: Cumulative; with focus > 0 the discharge ratio Q/(R A0) concentrates it along channels, so peaks depend on resolution through A0 (default the mean cell area).

condition: written to the surface HDF5 for restarts; each only with its block

fields.name: carbSedRate
fields.meaning: Clastic (non-carbonate) part of the previous step's marine deposit as a rate, read by the carbonate sedrate/turbidity controls of the next step. With carbonate.
fields.range: 0 to a few 1e-2 m/yr at deltas (examples median 2e-5, max 4e-2 m/yr).
fields.resolution: Rate over one dt.

fields.name: turbRate
fields.meaning: River mud carried through each cell by the previous step's marine routing, divided by cell area and dt: the source of the turbidity plume. Only when a factory uses turbidity with source transport.
fields.range: 0 to ~1 m/yr near mouths (examples median 2e-3, max 0.96 m/yr).
fields.resolution: Through-flow per cell area, so larger on smaller cells.

fields.name: pelCarry
fields.meaning: Pelagic carbonate (column 0) and clay (column 1) thickness below the deposit floor carried over to the next steps (shape lpoints x 2). With pelagic.
fields.range: 0 to DEPOSIT_FLOOR (1e-9 m).
fields.resolution: Round-off bookkeeping.

fields.name: marineSolute
fields.meaning: Marine solute reservoir per species (global array, identical on every rank, shape nspecies): cumulative river delivery to the ocean, drawn down by carbonate burial with carbonate_supply. With marine_coupling.
fields.range: Grows with time; examples 4e9 to 7e14; calibration dependent.
fields.resolution: Integrated over time, so independent of dt.

condition: with stratigraphic recording (output: strat interval set); written in h5/stratal.<step>.p<rank>.h5 at each output, one column per recorded layer (column 0 is the initial or bedrock layer)

fields.name: stratZ
fields.meaning: Surface elevation when the layer was recorded (paleo-elevation at deposition; the top layer follows the current surface until the next layer starts). Not updated by later uplift or flexure, only moved by plate advection.
fields.range: Same range as elev.
fields.resolution: One value per layer; layers last the strat interval.

fields.name: stratH
fields.meaning: Layer thickness after erosion and compaction (total, all lithologies). Column 0 holds the BEDROCK_SENTINEL 1e6 m infinite-bedrock layer when no strata file sets it.
fields.range: 0 to tens of m per layer (examples max 31-69 m); 1e6 in the sentinel column.
fields.resolution: Thickness per layer scales with the strat interval; peaks larger on finer meshes.

fields.name: phiS
fields.meaning: Porosity of the coarse sediment of the layer from the depth-porosity (compaction) curve.
fields.range: Below phi0s/phi0c (example 0.43-0.49).
fields.resolution: Depends on burial depth only.

fields.name: stratK
fields.meaning: Erodibility multiplier of the layer (1 for goSPL deposits; may differ for strata-file layers or soil mode).
fields.range: Usually 1.
fields.resolution: None.

fields.name: stratHf
fields.meaning: Fine (mud) thickness of the layer (lithology 0); fine fraction = stratHf / stratH. With dual lithology.
fields.range: 0 to stratH.
fields.resolution: As stratH.

fields.name: phiF
fields.meaning: Porosity of the fine sediment of the layer. With dual lithology.
fields.range: Below phi0f (example 0.60-0.63).
fields.resolution: Depends on burial depth.

fields.name: stratH_<name>
fields.meaning: Thickness of one additional lithology in the layer (strata: lithologies, or the carbonate lithologies reef, carb_sand, carb_mud); coarse clastic = stratH minus all piles.
fields.range: 0 to stratH (examples carbonate piles up to 1-7 m per layer).
fields.resolution: As stratH.

fields.name: phi_<name>
fields.meaning: Porosity of that lithology in the layer.
fields.range: Below the lithology's surface porosity (examples reef 0.20, carb_sand 0.45, carb_mud 0.65).
fields.resolution: Depends on burial depth.

fields.name: stratDuri
fields.meaning: Diagenetic induration degree archived in the layer. With the groundwater duricrust.
fields.range: 0 to 1.
fields.resolution: Per layer.

fields.name: stratCrustType
fields.meaning: Dominant solute species of the layer's crust (-1 = none). Integer as float64. With geochemistry.
fields.range: -1 to nspecies - 1.
fields.resolution: Categorical.

fields.name: stratCrustSource
fields.meaning: Dominant source region (provenance class) of the layer's crust chemistry (-1 = none). With geochemistry and provenance.
fields.range: -1 to provenance classes - 1.
fields.resolution: Categorical.

fields.name: stratP
fields.meaning: Per-layer per-provenance-class thickness (3-D array lpoints x layers x classes); sums to stratH. With the provenance block.
fields.range: 0 to stratH; 1e6 in the bedrock sentinel column.
fields.resolution: As stratH.
